matched_pairs.b_evidence_quote: We present a new method that views object detection as a direct set prediction problem.

The main ingredients of the new framework, called DEtection TRansformer or DETR, are a set-based global loss that forces unique predictions via bipartite matching, and a transformer encoder-decoder architecture.
All transformer weights are initialized with Xavier init [11], and the backbone is with ImageNet-pretrained ResNet model [15] from torchvision with frozen batchnorm layers.
We define the loss similarly to the losses of common object detectors, i.e. a linear combination of a negative log-likelihood for class prediction and a box loss defined later.
Overall, our box loss is Lbox(bi,ˆbσ(i)) defined as λiouLiou(bi,ˆbσ(i)) +λL1||bi− ˆbσ(i)||1 where λiou,λ L1∈ R are hyperparameters.
We evaluate DETR on one of the most popular object detection datasets, COCO [24], against a very competitive Faster R-CNN baseline [37].
